brother.definition: a brother is a male sibling.
examples: Her brother helped with the car.

bus.definition: a large road vehicle designed to carry many passengers.
examples: We took the bus to the city.

begin.definition: to come or go into existence or to start.
examples: They will begin soon.

bread.definition: a staple food made from flour and water that is baked.
examples: Fresh bread smells wonderful.

build.definition: to make something by putting parts together; to construct.
examples: We will build shelves for the room.

builder.definition: a person who builds things; a constructor.
examples: A skilled builder works on the project.

building.definition: the act or the structure of something being built.
examples: The building looks new.
The built house stands strong.

bright.definition: full of light; intelligent or quick-witted.
examples: The sun is bright today.

boil.definition: to heat a liquid until it becomes hot and bubbles appear.
examples: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes.

bake.definition: to cook by dry heat, usually in an oven.
examples: We bake cookies every Christmas.

ball.definition: a round object used in sports and games.
examples: They kicked the ball across the field.

bat.definition: a smooth wooden stick used in sports to hit the ball.
examples: The bat broke after the hit.

brook.definition: To tolerate or allow without objection.
examples: She will not brook interference in her plans.

bros.definition: Plural form of bro; informal for brothers or close male friends.
examples: The bros met up after class.

bro.definition: An informal term for a male friend or brother.
examples: Hey bro, want to grab a coffee?

bud.definition: A young shoot or bud of a plant; a friend in informal speech.
examples: A new bud appeared on the branch.

benevolent.definition: Kind and helpful toward others; showing goodwill.
examples: A benevolent donor funded the school.

benefactor.definition: A person who gives help or financial aid to another person or organization.
examples: Several benefactors supported the arts program.

benefit.definition: An advantage, improvement, or help gained from something.
examples: The new law provides several benefits.

benison.definition: A blessing; an expression of good wishes.
examples: The priest offered a benison at the ceremony.

boot.definition: To kick something with the foot; to start a computer or system.
examples: Boot up the computer before you begin.
That friendly bloke is our guide for the tour.

brusque.definition: Abrupt and ungracious in speech or manner.
examples: His brusque response offended several people.

blade.definition: The flat cutting part of a tool or weapon, such as a knife, sword, or saw.
examples: The blade of the knife gleamed in the light.

biology.definition: The science that studies living organisms.
examples: He wants to become a biology teacher.

bardic.definition: Relating to a bard; characteristic of a poet or minstrel.
examples: The festival featured bardic performances.
The buzz of the bees filled the garden.
I could hear the faint buzz of a fluorescent light.

buzz.definition: To make a buzzing sound; to vibrate with a low hum.
examples: A fly buzzed around the room all afternoon.
My phone buzzed in my pocket during the meeting.

bank.definition: a financial institution where people keep money and borrow money
examples: The bank is near the station.
I opened an account at a bank.

bank.definition: the side of a river or lake
examples: We sat on the bank of the river.
The ducks were near the bank.

bank.definition: to move or turn an aircraft so that it tilts to one side
examples: The pilot banked left.
The plane banks sharply during the turn.

bass.definition: a type of fish that lives in rivers or lakes
examples: We caught a bass in the lake.
Bass are popular for fishing.

bass.definition: a low musical voice or the low part of music
examples: He sings bass in the choir.
The song’s bass is very deep.

bass.definition: low in pitch, especially in music or voice
examples: She has a bass voice.

bowl.definition: a container that is round and usually open at the top, used for food or liquids
examples: He ate soup from a bowl.
Please pass me the bowl.

book.definition: a set of written or printed pages that are bound together
examples: I finished the book last night.
Do you have that book in paperback?

book.definition: to reserve a place or service in advance
examples: I booked a table for two.
She booked her flight online.

baker.definition: a person who makes bread, cakes, and other baked food
examples: The baker sells fresh bread every morning.
She works as a baker.

blue.definition: having the color of the sky on a clear day
examples: He has blue eyes.
The car is blue.

ballad.definition: a song or poem that tells a story, often in a slow and emotional way
examples: The ballad tells the story of a sailor.
We listened to an old ballad.

brawny.definition: strong and muscular, especially in appearance
examples: He has a brawny build.
A brawny worker lifted the box easily.

brisk.definition: quick and energetic, or pleasantly cold
examples: We walked at a brisk pace.
It was a brisk morning.
She spoke briskly and clearly.

banana.definition: a long yellow fruit that grows in clusters
examples: Do you want a banana?
She ate a banana for breakfast.
The doctor said the tumor is benign.
He had a benign smile.

buddy.definition: a friend, especially a male friend, in informal speech
examples: My buddy helped me move.
We are good buddies.

blunder.definition: A serious mistake caused by carelessness or poor judgment
examples: Leaving the door open was a blunder.
It was a blunder to sign without reading the terms.
He blundered by sending the email to the wrong person.
I blundered and booked the wrong date.

bungle.definition: To do something badly because you make mistakes
examples: They bungled the task and had to start over.
I bungled the calculation and got the wrong answer.

bleak.definition: Cold, empty, and unpleasant; also, offering little hope
examples: The bleak landscape looked icy and silent.
She felt bleak about her chances.

behold.definition: To see something, especially something impressive
examples: Behold the view from the top of the hill.
The crowd stood still to behold the parade.

bolter.definition: A person or animal that suddenly escapes or runs away
examples: The police caught the bolter near the station.
A bolter escaped from the yard.

blunt.definition: Not sharp; having a dull edge or tip
examples: Be careful, the knife is blunt.
The blade is blunt, so it won’t cut well.

blunt.definition: Direct and not trying to be polite or soft
examples: He gave a blunt answer.
Her blunt criticism surprised everyone.

blueprint.definition: A detailed plan or drawing for building a structure or doing a project
examples: The engineers followed the blueprint for the bridge.
We reviewed the blueprint before starting work.

beguiling.definition: Charming and attractive, sometimes in a way that tricks people
examples: Her smile was beguiling, but her story didn’t add up.
He used beguiling words to avoid the truth.

benchmark.definition: A standard or reference point used for comparison
examples: This score is our benchmark for improvement.
The team set a benchmark for response times.

brand.definition: A particular company’s product name or identity, often with its own design and reputation
examples: That brand is known for good quality.
We chose a new brand for the campaign.

brand.definition: To mark or identify something by putting a name or symbol on it
examples: They branded the boxes with the delivery date.
The company brands its products with a logo.

beget.definition: To cause something, especially an outcome such as a feeling or problem
examples: The delay beget ed more confusion.
New rules can beget unexpected results.

barbed.definition: Having sharp points; also, said in a sharp or insulting way
examples: A barbed wire fence surrounds the property.
He made a barbed comment about her accent.

blizzard.definition: A severe snowstorm with strong winds and low visibility
examples: A blizzard forced the flight to cancel.
We stayed indoors during the blizzard.

brawl.definition: A noisy, violent fight, often involving several people
examples: A brawl started outside the bar.
The brawl lasted only a few minutes.

brawl.definition: To fight in a noisy and violent way
examples: Two groups brawled after the game.
They brawled over a misunderstanding.

bicker.definition: To argue about small issues repeatedly
examples: They bicker over money every month.
Stop bickering and focus on the task.

broadsword.definition: A large sword with a wide blade
examples: The warrior held a broadsword in both hands.
A broadsword can be heavy and difficult to control.

beam.definition: A long thick piece of metal or wood used to support a structure
examples: The roof collapsed because the main beam was damaged.
They installed a new beam in the ceiling.

beam.definition: To send out light, radio signals, or energy in a direction
examples: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
A spotlight beamed across the room.

banter.definition: Playful and friendly conversation, often with jokes
examples: They spent the evening in banter and laughter.
There was friendly banter between the two teams.
They bantered while waiting for the train.
The friends bantered about sports.

beseech.definition: to ask someone for something in an urgent or emotional way
examples: She beseeched him to stay.
They beseeched the court for help.

belittle.definition: to make someone feel less important, capable, or worthy
examples: He belittled her ideas during the meeting.
Don’t belittle students who ask questions.

byline.definition: the line under a news story that shows the writer’s name
examples: Her name appeared in the byline.
The byline listed the reporter and editor.

bewilder.definition: to confuse someone so they do not understand what is happening
examples: The instructions bewildered me.
Her sudden change of plans bewildered everyone.

blemish.definition: a small mark that spoils the appearance of something
examples: The report has a small blemish in the last paragraph.
She tried to cover the blemish.

blemish.definition: to spoil the appearance or quality of something
examples: The stain blemished the shirt.
The scandal blemished his reputation.

baffle.definition: to confuse someone strongly so they cannot understand what to do
examples: The instructions baffled me.
Her sudden silence baffled everyone.

blather.definition: to talk too much in a foolish or unhelpful way
examples: He kept blathering about unrelated topics.
Stop blathering and get to the point.
I can’t stand the blather in that show.
His speech was full of blather.

blurry.definition: not clear or sharp in appearance or meaning
examples: The text is blurry; please focus the camera.
I have a blurry memory of that day.

birth.definition: the time when a baby is born
examples: Her birth was a difficult event.
They celebrated his birth with a party.

buoyant.definition: Able to float and stay up on water
examples: The toy is buoyant, so it does not sink.
Buoyant materials are often used in life jackets.

buoyant.definition: Cheerful and confident, especially when facing problems
examples: Despite the delay, he stayed buoyant.
Her buoyant mood helped the group keep working.

bolster.definition: To support something and make it stronger or more likely to succeed
examples: The new evidence bolstered her argument.
They added more funding to bolster the program.

bolster.definition: Support that helps something stay strong or improve performance
examples: The report served as a bolster for the campaign.
